items.text: **Autopilot, for a channel that runs by itself.** Settings has a new Autopilot row: off, calm, steady or lively. While it is on, the field keeps changing with nobody touching it: it rolls the dice, draws, adds and drops G-code drawings, turns on drawing motion, pulses to the grid and nudges the tempo, one gesture every so often (calm about a minute, lively about every fifteen seconds), never holding more than the mood's cap of drawings and voices. It pauses while you touch, and carries on after.

**On air.** Open the page with `?autopilot=calm`, `steady` or `lively` and it starts itself, starts the sound, hides every control and restarts the score if it ever stops. That address is what a streaming program's browser source (OBS, say) points at.

**The grid pulses the drawings.** Every grid note strike now kicks a short pulse, and each drawing (the main one and each one you added) has its own four amounts for it on its remote: swell (size), quicken (speed), twist (rotation) and vertex (strengthens the vertex effects). Set to nothing they do nothing.

**A dice roll can swap a drawing.** The main drawing swaps on a roll with "by hand / on dice" and a chance (always, mostly, half, sometimes); an added drawing has its own switch. They take the next drawing from the ticked set in the order you choose: bag, in order, bounce (up the set and back), random, or stay on one.

**Two ways to morph.** Through a line (every vertex flattens onto a line, then opens into the next) or a straight blend (every vertex glides to its place). Chosen in the Change settings, and per drawing on its remote. It applies to dice rolls, the Form, the swing and the timers alike.

**Several G-code drawings can be picked.** Tap any drawing's line to select it (the hit area follows the whole line now, not just points along it), tap well away from every drawing to let go, and the previous and next arrows now step between the drawings (the main one, then each one you added) instead of cycling a drawing's own handles.
**Lines glow when you can pick them.** In the G-code editor, a drawing's line takes a soft warm tint under the mouse, so you see what a tap will choose.
**The drawer no longer chooses for you.** Opening the + drawer used to drop a random drawing on the screen first; now it waits for your pick.

**The bar stays centred when the stage is narrow.** On a wide desktop screen, squeezing the frame narrower than the bar left the bar starting at the frame's left edge and running off to the right. It now sits centred under the frame whatever its width.

**The Room.** The field's cube now goes wall, stage, room. In the Room you stand in the middle (a grey listener, nose to the front), the speakers you chose (4 or 8, or headphones) are drawn around you, and a sound is heard where it is drawn: in front, behind, to either side, all the way round. A sound riding a G-code shape circles you as the shape moves. Far from the middle is quieter, darker and wetter. Speakers your device cannot play are drawn hollow. The grid comes to the Room next, as its own switch.

**Choosing a drawing is visual.** The + now opens a narrow drawer on the left, in the remote's look: every drawing is its own picture, in a scrolling grid, sets along the top, shapes at the foot. Tap one and it is added (or swaps the main drawing, with the first button) and the drawer closes. Tap outside or press Esc to close. The tools that were hidden in the old panel (put the drawing back, keep it, vertex effects) sit under the three dots.

**A ghosted path now really goes.** A ghost kept alive by a sound that had already let go of it (for example after you dropped that sound elsewhere) stayed for ever. Only a sound still being edited keeps its ghost now.

**Chalk, not a cut.** When a sound with a path is taken away, its line wears away in patches and lifts off as dust over about three bars (6 to 24 seconds, by tempo). It only draws; nothing plays, and Undo leaves no trace.

**No more flash of loose controls on a reload.** Before the home screen came up, a jumble of not-yet-working controls showed for a moment. The page now stays dark until the launch cover is up (and lifts itself after 5 seconds whatever happens).

**Pencil on a held note: the level answers.** Dragging a held note shaped only the reverb with the Pencil, because its pressure had replaced the vertical drag as the level. Up and down always sets the level now, and pressing harder adds to it.
**The remote is tighter.** Its buttons are flush grid cells with hairlines between them, like the halo on the grid, and no frame around the icon column.

**Dots for choices, bars for levels.** A button you step through (source, move, effect) now shows one dot per option, the chosen one lit, and it pops as you step. Tap steps on; drag steps too. A level (volume, tone) keeps its bar. Previous, next and plain buttons carry no line at all.
**The cell halo has a handle.** Drag it onto the next cell and the halo reopens there, no tapping away and back. Arrow keys on the handle step to the neighbour.
